translation: The Tian Yuan Ji Da Lun (天元紀大論) says: When the numbers reach their extreme and the way is not confused, one may be called clear-sighted. As for what is called the functions of drugs: warm and cool differ, cold and heat are opposite, dryness and dampness have different roots—this has already been discussed above. (The above pushes the discussion of the transformation of qi and sets forth the root and branch; it completes the principle of the first half of the treatise, and is the third section. Below, the treatment methods of supplementing and draining by the five flavors are discussed, bringing the whole treatise to a close; this is the fourth section.)
translator_notes: 天元紀大論 kept as chapter name; parenthetical section markers preserved.
